text.p: Philippine National Bank net income this year is targetted at 2.1 billion pesos, compared to last year's recurring net of 1.7 billion, senior executive vice president Valentine Araneta told reporters on Wednesday.
The rise is based on projected earnings from banking operations, fees and underwriting activities, he added.
The bank reported last week its net income in the first quarter reached 467 million pesos compared with 340 million in the year-earlier period.
"We like to pursue loans in manufacturing, credits in growth areas outside of Metro Manila, trade finance, and housing for the C and D (income) market," Araneta said.
But he insisted the bank would maintain a prudent lending policy in the face of a fast growing economy.
"Our selectivity is always influenced by the market. Sectoral exposures are always monitored so we can expand and pursue with caution," Araneta said.
Bank officials also said the bank is forming a leasing company and will be spinning off its investment banking division into a separate unit in order to give it greater flexibility.
Araneta said the separate investment house will have an authorised capital stock of 1.0 billion pesos with a paid-up capital of 500 million.
The leasing company is expected to have 40 percent equity participation from a Japanese institution, he said. It will be capitalised at $5.0 million.
